current.jp: 駅の前に警官がいます
current.kana: えきのまえにけいかんがいます

structure_explanation.en: The sentence describes the existence of a living being, which is why it uses the verb います (from いる). '駅の前' means 'the front of the station' (の links station + front), and に marks that point as the place where something is. '警官が' uses が to present the police officer as that which exists there.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase descreve a existência de algo vivo, por isso usa o verbo います (de いる). '駅の前' significa 'a frente da estação' (の liga estação + frente), e に marca esse ponto como o lugar onde algo está. '警官が' usa が para apresentar o policial como aquilo que existe ali.

translation_literal.en: As for in front of the station (の前に), there is a policeman (が).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Na frente da estação (の前に), policial (が) existe.

translation.en: There's a police officer in front of the station.
translation.pt-BR: Tem um policial na frente da estação.

note.en: connective stem (連用形) of いる, linking to ます
note.pt-BR: raiz conectiva (連用形) de いる, ligando-se a ます

objections.objection: lit_pt was corrected to a plain locative ("Na frente da estação (の前に)...") but lit_en still reads "As for in front of the station (の前に), there is a policeman (が)." The sentence contains no は; 駅の前 is marked by に. The "As for" topic device therefore still misteaches に as a topic marker, and the en/pt literals now mirror two different structures for the same sentence.
objections.auditor_hint: In front of the station (の前に), there is a policeman (が).

current.jp: 弁護士が接見に行きました
current.kana: べんごしがせっけんにいきました

structure_explanation.en: The structure is [subject]が [action noun]に 行きました, the pattern 'to go do something': the verbal noun 接見 + に + the movement verb 行く expresses the purpose of the trip ('to go to the interview'). Here 接見 is in the legal sense of a lawyer's interview with the detained person. 行きました is the polite past form of 行く (to go).
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura é [sujeito]が [nome de ação]に 行きました, o padrão 'ir fazer algo': o nome verbal 接見 + に + verbo de movimento 行く expressa o propósito do deslocamento ('ir para a entrevista'). Aqui 接見 está no sentido jurídico de entrevista do advogado com a pessoa detida. 行きました é a forma polida do passado de 行く (ir).

translation_literal.en: As for the lawyer (が), went to the interview/audience (接見に行きました).
translation_literal.pt-BR: O advogado (が, sujeito) foi para a entrevista (接見に行きました).

translation.en: The lawyer went to visit the detained client.
translation.pt-BR: O advogado foi visitar o cliente detido.

note.en: 連用形 form いき of 行く, linking to ます
note.pt-BR: forma 連用形 いき de 行く, ligando-se a ます

note.en: 連用形 form まし of ます, before た
note.pt-BR: forma 連用形 まし de ます, antes de た

note.en: た = past, forming ました
note.pt-BR: た = passado, formando ました

objections.objection: lit_pt was fixed to "O advogado (が, sujeito) foi...", but lit_en is unchanged: "As for the lawyer (が), went to the interview/audience (接見に行きました)." It applies the topic-は mirror to a が-marked subject - the very defect the op names, and the op text quotes lit_en explicitly. The two literal fields now contradict each other on the particle analysis.
objections.auditor_hint: The lawyer (が, subject) went to the interview/audience (接見に行きました).

current.kana: まいつきははにてがみをかく

structure_explanation.en: The sentence has the time adverb 毎月 (every month, the target) followed by two complements before the verb: 母に (to the mother, recipient marked by に) and 手紙を (letter, object marked by を). The verb 書く (to write) is at the end, in dictionary form, expressing a recurring habit.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase começa com 毎月 (todo mês), o alvo desta sentença, e tem dois complementos antes do verbo: 母に (para a mãe, destinatário marcado por に) e 手紙を (carta, objeto marcado por を). O verbo 書く (escrever) fica no fim, na forma de dicionário, indicando um costume recorrente.

translation_literal.en: Every month, to my mother, as for a letter, I write (one).
translation_literal.pt-BR: Todo mês, à mãe, carta (objeto), (eu) escrevo.

translation.en: Every month I write a letter to my mom.
translation.pt-BR: Todo mês escrevo uma carta para a minha mãe.

note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário (presente/não-passado) de 書く

objections.objection: lit_pt was corrected to "carta (objeto)", but lit_en still reads "Every month, to my mother, as for a letter, I write (one)." 手紙 is the direct object marked by を (the explanation says "objeto marcado por を"), so "as for a letter" still teaches を as a topic marker, and it no longer matches the fixed pt-BR mirror.
objections.auditor_hint: Every month, to my mother, a letter (object), I write (one).

current.jp: この港から貿易が始まりました
current.kana: このみなとからぼうえきがはじまりました

structure_explanation.en: The starting point is この港 (this port), marked by から (from / starting from). The subject is 貿易 (trade), marked by が. The verb 始まる (to begin, intransitive) appears in 始まりました, polite past (ます + た). The 連体詞 この (this) directly modifies 港.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O ponto de partida é この港 (este porto), marcado por から (a partir de / desde). O sujeito é 貿易 (comércio), marcado por が. O verbo 始まる (começar, intransitivo) aparece em 始まりました, passado polido (ます + た). 連体詞 この (este) modifica diretamente 港.

translation_literal.pt-BR: A partir deste porto, quanto ao comércio, começou.

translation.pt-BR: O comércio começou a partir deste porto.

note.en: stem of 始まる (godan verb, intransitive) in connective form to take ます
note.pt-BR: raiz de 始まる (verbo godan, intransitivo) na forma conectiva para receber ます

note.en: the まし form of the auxiliary ます, base for the auxiliary た
note.pt-BR: forma まし do auxiliar ます, base para o auxiliar た

note.en: auxiliary た, marking the past tense
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た, marca o tempo passado

objections.objection: translation_literal.pt-BR is 'A partir deste porto, quanto ao comércio, começou.' — the 'quanto a X' device is reserved for the topic particle は, but 貿易 here is marked by が. The record's own explanation calls it 'O sujeito é 貿易 (comércio), marcado por が', and lit_en shows no topic device at all ('From this port, trade began.'), so lit_en and lit_pt do not describe the same structure. This is exactly the defect the batch fixed in sent:gen-baae64313e3e and sent:gen-b5c5f20e6a99; leaving it here ships the contradiction and teaches が = topic. Untouched by the ops on this record (which only addressed tokens[6].note).
objections.auditor_hint: A partir deste porto, o comércio [が] começou.

current.kana: かのじょわいそがしいようです

structure_explanation.en: The pattern 〜様です here comes after an i-adjective (忙しい), which links directly to 様 in dictionary form: 忙しい様です ('she seems busy'). Rewrite around the corrected jp: 'ようです here expresses appearance/conjecture based on evidence; after an i-adjective it attaches directly to the dictionary form (忙しいようです = she seems busy).', with the sense of appearance/conjecture. The topic 彼女 (she) is marked by は.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: O padrão 〜様です vem aqui após um adjetivo-い (忙しい), que se liga direto a 様 na forma de dicionário: 忙しい様です ('parece estar ocupada'). Rewrite: 'ようです aqui expressa aparência/conjectura baseada em evidência; após um adjetivo-い, liga-se direto à forma de dicionário (忙しいようです = parece estar ocupada).', com sentido de aparência/conjectura. O tópico 彼女 (ela) é marcado por は.

translation_literal.en: As for her, she looks (like she is) busy.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto a ela, ocupada tem aparência de (estar).

note.en: い-adjective 忙しい in the dictionary form, linking directly to 様
note.pt-BR: adjetivo-い 忙しい na forma de dicionário, ligando-se direto a 様

role.en: head of the 様です pattern (conjecture from evidence)
role.pt-BR: núcleo do padrão 様です (conjectura por evidência)
